(for posterity): Read my claims again along with what the paper shows. I was specific and the paper supports them.

And, it def hasn't failed but I don't have time to educate you.

Watch this if you care to: https://youtu.be/BeRjTtKFlVM

Uuuh, I think that source contradicts your claims and supports the consensus? NK has messed up big time in the past decades and SK is doing great. Communism didn't just fail in one single experiment, it failed in all of them, China, Soviet, Cuba, NK, etc

> Also, north korea had an average economic growth higher than south korea for a huge chunk of the time since the korean war, and, for a long time had a higher gdp per capita.

Big if true

You used a lot of small words and were very wrong.

Capitalism very much improved upon feudalist systems. Capitalism is a very large step forward from that. Socialist systems, however, account for the vast majority of the uplift out of poverty in the last century (worldbank, of all sources https://openknowledge.worldbank.org/server/api/core/bitstrea... ). Also, north korea had an average economic growth higher than south korea for a huge chunk of the time since the korean war, and, for a long time had a higher gdp per capita. This is especially impressive as NK was bombed so badly that it was said that "Pyongyang was an ashen moonscape." Also, you're making the mistake of confusing a singular socialist experiment with socialism as a concept.

> [socialism] is the most direct way to satisfy diverse value priors apriori, as it minimizes many wasteful/harmful social costs, directs value to where it is need, is a stable and attractive basin when considering relative actor value prior divergence as people align towards shared community/society goals over time

You used a lot of big words but capitalism has proven to be most effective at allocating resources with its invisible hand and it's not even close. See South Korea vs north Korea.

source.text:
As a relatively unknown ex principal AI researcher (with a focus in computational creativity, machine learning, and more), yes they should.

Further, we need socialism/Communism and we need it yesterday. Exercise your right to freedom of choice in political engagement in this country, and find a socialist or communist party active near you and sign up. If you're not ready for that, join the DSA (which isn't actually socialist by the more traditional definitions, but, is close enough to learn how organize and engage with your community) and find the people who lean communist the furthest in your chapter and make friends. Avoid anarchists calling for anarchism before socialism: anarchism within capitalism segments communities and focus and makes any movement less capable of accumulating the necessary power to make effective change to the system. Anarchism makes more sense in late-stage (likely automated) socialism/communism, as the effective needs for shared resources (such as infrastructure, utilities, defense, etc) are solved by both social norms, systemic factors, and, again, likely future automation, given the state of things.

Socialism/Communism (the difference is only that Communists believe in removing the idea of a nationstate completely after socialism has taken firm root globally) makes sense from a multi-actor value optimization standpoint, as well: it's the most direct way to satisfy diverse value priors apriori, as it minimizes many wasteful/harmful social costs, directs value to where it is need, is a stable and attractive basin when considering relative actor value prior divergence as people align towards shared community/society goals over time, and reduces unintentional/harmful inter-actor competition. Socialism also minimizes logistical factors/costs by accounting for systems as a whole in order to increase efficiency. Further, there are alternatives to capitalism that still have markets, and, there's a lot to be said postively about said market systems within socialism/communism. For example, the Chinese party treats its markets similar to how a technition might control a nuclear reactor: they look at various metrics like competition, community health, worker rights, efficiency, tech-factors, etc and add and remove control mechanisms in order to achieve greater harmony between the metrics and societal good, while keeping final control in the hands of the political system instead of the capitalists leading the market.

They achieve this clean separation of personal finances and finance based power accumulation from governmental officials and agencies by distinguishing enterprise (including State Owned Enterprises [SOE]) from SCIOCs (think financial instutitions like a governmental aligned blackrock) and banning direct participation in ownership and accumulation in the market from any government officials, while keeping their SCIOCs under the direction of highly-trained Communist leadership as the financial intermediary system, which keeps their money out of politics, while still being able to enact the will of their people through them via policy direction on the SCIOCs. This is all to say, a better future is possible, we just gotta make it happen.
